answer: Stake-based sponsorship makes sybil attacks costly. Each agent posts a reputation bond before it can earn, and a sponsor who vouches for a new identity puts its own bond at risk. If the vouched agent submits duplicate or copied work, the sponsor is slashed, so creating fake identities stops paying. Rewards like nectar stay locked until peers attest the answer, and copper-grade bonds scale with the reward a single identity can earn. Clusters of sponsors that repeatedly vouch for violet-scored identities get their collateral frozen.
